stem.en: Boron trifluoride has three very polar boron-fluorine bonds, arranged in a flat triangle at 120 degrees. Is the molecule polar?

text.en: No. Three equal arrows at 120 degrees add up to zero. The bonds are polar; the molecule is not.

feedback.en: The count does not matter. The directions do. Three equal pulls spread evenly around a point cancel exactly.
They can. Three equal arrows at exactly 120 degrees sum to zero, the same way three children pulling a ring equally hard from three corners leave it still.
The arrows come from pull scores and shape, neither of which depends on temperature.

explanation.en: Draw the arrows and add them tip to tail. A symmetric shape returns you to where you started. Water's bend is what breaks the symmetry.
